name: 5-Persona Advisory Board
about: Agent skill that stress-tests decisions through five strategy lenses
description: 5-Persona Advisory Board is a portable agent skill that walks important decisions through product, capital, scale, offer, and future-self lenses inspired by public business principles. Founders use it as a structured devil's advocate before launches, pricing moves, or pivots.

name: A Soft Murmur
about: Mix ambient sounds like rain, wind, and fire into your own soundscape
description: A Soft Murmur lets you blend multiple ambient sound layers — rain, thunder, wind, fire, and more — each with its own volume slider, to build a custom background soundscape. It's used for focus, relaxation, sleep, and masking distracting noise.

name: Activepieces
about: Open-source Zapier alternative with a visual workflow builder
description: Activepieces is a self-hostable automation platform with a polished visual builder and a growing connector library. It sits beside n8n and Zapier for teams that want no-code workflows with a friendlier UI than n8n's node canvas.

name: Adobe Acrobat
about: The standard PDF editor, reader, and e-sign suite
description: Adobe Acrobat creates, edits, signs, and converts PDFs across desktop, web, and mobile. It is what most people mean by a PDF tool; Stirling PDF, iLovePDF, and PDFescape cover lighter or self-hosted paths.

name: Adobe Podcast Enhance Speech
about: Free AI tool that cleans noisy, echoey audio to studio quality
description: Adobe Podcast's Enhance Speech tool uses AI to strip background noise, echo, and room reverb from a recording, turning phone or laptop-mic audio into near-studio quality. It's free and widely used by podcasters and creators who recorded audio outside a proper studio setup, distinct from Auphonic's leveling/loudness focus.

name: AFFiNE
about: Open-source notes, docs, and whiteboard in one canvas
description: AFFiNE is a local-first workspace that mixes documents with an infinite whiteboard. Search Notion alternative plus canvas and this is the hybrid; AppFlowy stays the closer Notion clone and Excalidraw the dedicated whiteboard.

name: AirForShare
about: Cross-platform local file sharing between devices, AirDrop-style
description: AirForShare enables local file sharing between devices across different platforms without needing a cloud upload, similar in spirit to PairDrop and Apple's AirDrop. Verify the current URL and product details before publishing — could not confidently confirm this entry against an authoritative source.

name: Alcove
about: Dynamic Island-style HUD for Mac
description: Alcove puts a Dynamic Island-like notch HUD on the Mac for notifications, live activities, and gestures. Search dynamic island mac or mac notch hud.

name: AlternativeTo
about: Crowd-sourced database of software alternatives, filterable by platform and license
description: AlternativeTo is a crowd-sourced platform where users discover alternatives to software and apps they already know, filterable by platform, license type, and pricing model. It's especially useful for finding open-source or free replacements for paid mainstream software.

name: AltTab
about: Windows-style window switcher for macOS
description: AltTab brings a thumbnail window switcher to the Mac, closer to Windows Alt-Tab than macOS's app-only Command-Tab. It is the standard fix when you want to jump between windows, not just apps.

name: Ambient Music Mod
about: Pixel Now Playing music recognition on other Androids
description: Ambient Music Mod ports Google Pixel Now Playing so non-Pixel phones can identify music playing around you. Search now playing android or pixel ambient music.

name: Amphetamine
about: Keeps a Mac awake on demand
description: Amphetamine prevents sleep with triggers, sessions, and a menu-bar toggle, the usual Caffeine successor. Search keep mac awake or prevent sleep mac.

name: Animated Drawings
about: Upload a drawn character, Meta AI rigs and animates it moving
description: Animated Drawings, a Meta AI research demo, takes a photo of a hand-drawn character — often a kid's drawing — and automatically rigs and animates it so it walks and moves. It's built as a fun, accessible way to bring drawings to life without any animation skill.

name: AnswerThePublic
about: Visualizes the questions people search around a keyword
description: AnswerThePublic pulls autocomplete search-query data and visualizes it as a map of questions, prepositions, and comparisons people search around a given keyword. It's used by marketers and content creators for SEO research and content ideation.

name: Anydoc
about: Converts Word, PPT, Excel, EPUB, and PDF to clean Markdown
description: Anydoc is a Rust document converter from the Firecrawl team with Node and Python bindings. It turns office files, EPUBs, and PDFs into clean Markdown for RAG and agent pipelines, covering more formats than PDF-only tools like Marker.

name: AOS-CE
about: Agent OS with WASM-isolated capsules for safe capability growth
description: AOS-CE is an agent operating environment where new capabilities ship as WASM-isolated capsules instead of arbitrary shell access. Builders use it when they want agents that can extend themselves without handing models an unconstrained root shell.

name: Apache Maka
about: Incubating local-first agent workspace with append-only execution logs
description: Apache Maka is an incubator project building a local-first workspace where agent runs leave durable, append-only execution logs you can audit and replay. It overlaps coding assistants like Cursor but emphasizes traceable agent sessions on your own machine.

name: AppFlowy
about: Open-source Notion alternative for notes, docs, and databases
description: AppFlowy is a self-hostable workspace app combining notes, wikis, and databases with a Notion-like editing experience. It's aimed at teams and individuals who want full data ownership instead of a cloud-only SaaS notetaking tool.

name: Archify
about: Agent skill for architecture, sequence, and data-flow diagrams
description: Archify is an agent skill that produces verifiable architecture, workflow, sequence, and lifecycle diagrams as self-contained HTML with motion and clean export. Install it when you want agents to draw system diagrams instead of dumping Mermaid into a chat.

name: Are.na
about: Visual bookmarking and moodboard tool for collaborative research
description: Are.na is a platform for collecting, organizing, and connecting images, links, and text into visual blocks and channels, designed for research, moodboarding, and collaborative idea development. It's popular with designers, artists, and researchers who think visually.

name: Asana
about: Work management for tasks, projects, and team workflows
description: Asana is work-management software for assigning tasks, mapping projects, and tracking who is doing what by when, with optional AI teammates inside those workflows. It is leaner than ClickUp's all-in-one workspace — project tracking first, not a replacement for every app.

name: aShellYou
about: Local terminal and ADB shell for Android
description: aShellYou is a Material You terminal for running local commands and ADB on Android. Power users use it as the phone-side counterpart to a desktop terminal like Ghostty.

name: Atlas Obscura
about: Curated database of obscure and unusual travel destinations
description: Atlas Obscura catalogs offbeat, hidden, and unusual places worldwide — from abandoned sites to strange museums — curated by a community of contributors. It's built for travelers seeking destinations off the typical tourist path.

name: Auphonic
about: Automated audio post-production for podcasts and voice recordings
description: Auphonic automates audio post-production tasks like leveling, noise reduction, and loudness normalization, primarily for podcasters and voice recording creators. It removes the need for manual audio engineering knowledge to get broadcast-quality sound.

name: Aura
about: Gallery of 200+ CSS ambient gradient backgrounds
description: Aura is a collection of ready-made CSS gradient backgrounds for ambient UI backdrops and hero sections. Designers grab presets instead of hand-tuning radial and mesh gradients — unrelated to Aura Code, the separate terminal coding agent.

name: Aura Code
about: Model-agnostic terminal coding agent with memory and Telegram control
description: Aura Code is an autonomous coding agent with persistent memory, a terminal UI, and optional Telegram remote control across many LLM providers. It is unrelated to Aura, the CSS gradient gallery — this is a full agent product in the Claude Code lane.

name: Auto Cursor
about: One-handed pointer for large Android phones
description: Auto Cursor puts an on-screen cursor you pull from the edge so you can tap the far side of a large phone with one hand. Search one-handed android or reachability pointer; official site is autocursor.toneiv.eu, not the Cursor IDE.

name: AutoDraw
about: Doodle something rough, AI guesses it and offers clean icon replacements
description: AutoDraw, a Google experiment, uses machine learning to recognize what you're sketching and suggests polished icon-style replacements you can drop straight in. It's built for people who can't draw but want a clean visual fast, no artistic skill required.

name: Awesome GPT Image 2
about: Prompt-template library and agent skill for image generation
description: Awesome GPT Image 2 bundles prompt templates and an installable skill for getting consistent results from GPT image models. Creators use it when they want reusable prompt recipes instead of one-off experimentation in Google AI Studio or ChatGPT.

name: Behance
about: Adobe's portfolio platform for showcasing creative work
description: Behance is Adobe's platform for creatives to publish and discover portfolios spanning illustration, photography, UI/UX, branding, and more. It's a standard destination for hiring, inspiration, and building a public creative body of work.

name: Bento
about: PowerPoint alternative shipped as a single self-contained HTML file
description: Bento is presentation software that runs entirely from one HTML file you can email, host, or open offline. There is no install step and no server — the deck is the software, which makes it unusually portable for talks and demos.

name: Bitwarden
about: Open-source password manager
description: Bitwarden is an open-source password manager that stores and syncs credentials, generates strong passwords, and supports self-hosting for users who want full control over their data. It's a widely trusted, audited alternative to closed-source password managers.

name: Blip
about: Direct multi-gigabit file transfer between devices without cloud storage or size limits
description: Blip sends files and multi-gigabyte folders directly between Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android devices without uploading them to cloud storage or compressing them into archives. It streams transfers in real time, automatically resumes interrupted connections, and encrypts traffic in transit.

name: blobatar
about: Deterministic geometric avatars generated from any string
description: blobatar turns a username or seed string into a consistent geometric avatar without network calls. It is a fun identicon generator in the same spirit as This Person Does Not Exist or AutoDraw — small, deterministic, and shareable.

name: Buge App Manager
about: Android app and permission manager that uses Shizuku
description: Buge App Manager inspects installed apps, permissions, and related system details with Shizuku privileges. Search android app manager or permission manager shizuku.

name: Button Mapper
about: Remap Android hardware buttons to apps and actions
description: Button Mapper assigns tap, double-tap, and long-press actions to volume keys, Bixby, and other hardware buttons. Search remap android buttons or flashlight on volume key and this is the usual Play Store answer.

name: Buzz
about: Self-hostable workspace where humans and AI agents share rooms
description: Buzz from Block is a self-hosted collaboration space built on Nostr where people and agents participate in shared rooms. Teams experiment with it when they want agent coworkers inside a chat-shaped product instead of a solo terminal agent.

name: Cadran
about: Customizable clock faces rendered on the macOS desktop wallpaper layer
description: Cadran renders analog, digital, and data-driven clock faces directly onto the macOS wallpaper layer behind desktop icons rather than in floating widgets or windows. It includes live weather complications, dynamic sky backgrounds that shift with sunrise and sunset, multi-display support, and native screensaver mode.

name: Cal.DIY
about: Self-hosted scheduling and booking tool, a Cal.com/Calendly alternative
description: Cal.DIY is a self-hostable scheduling tool for booking meetings and managing availability, offering an open-source alternative to hosted scheduling SaaS like Calendly.

name: CamelCamelCamel
about: Amazon price history tracker with drop alerts
description: CamelCamelCamel tracks price history for millions of Amazon products and sends alerts when a price drops to a target threshold. It helps shoppers avoid overpaying by showing whether a current price is actually a good deal relative to historical lows and highs.

name: Canva
about: Drag-and-drop design tool with templates for social, print, and presentations
description: Canva is a template-driven design platform that lets non-designers create social media graphics, presentations, print materials, and videos through a simple drag-and-drop editor. It's the go-to tool for fast, template-based design versus Photopea's pro-editor approach.

name: Cap
about: Open-source screen recorder, a Loom alternative
description: Cap is an open-source screen recording and sharing app for quick async video. Teams self-host or use the cloud when they want Loom-style clips without a closed SaaS lock-in.

name: CaskHub
about: Native GUI for Homebrew Casks on Mac
description: CaskHub is an open-source Mac app for browsing, installing, and updating Homebrew Casks without the terminal. Use it when you want a GUI for GUI apps from brew; Tappie covers formulae and casks together.

name: CC-Switch
about: Desktop app to switch providers for Claude Code, Codex, and similar CLIs
description: CC-Switch is a small desktop utility for juggling API keys, endpoints, and profiles across terminal coding agents like Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. It saves people who bounce between providers from hand-editing config files every session.

name: ChatGPT
about: OpenAI's hosted chat interface for GPT models
description: ChatGPT is the consumer chat app for OpenAI models, used for writing, Q&A, coding help, and image generation in the browser and mobile apps. Search chatgpt or ai chat and this is the primary hit; Jan and Open WebUI cover local/self-hosted alternatives.

name: Chonkie
about: RAG text-chunking library for splitting documents intelligently
description: Chonkie provides chunking strategies purpose-built for retrieval pipelines — semantic splits, token-aware boundaries, and helpers RAG engineers reach for instead of naive fixed-size slicing. It is a small library, but a common dependency in document QA stacks.

name: Claude Code
about: Anthropic's coding agent for the terminal, IDE, and GitHub
description: Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent that works in the terminal, IDE, browser, and GitHub — reading the repo, editing files, running commands, and opening PRs. It requires a paid Claude plan (Pro and up) rather than a free tier, and it is the CLI-first counterpart to Cursor's editor.

name: Claude Code Plugins
about: Official Anthropic marketplace of Claude Code plugins
description: Claude Code Plugins is Anthropic's official registry of plugins that extend Claude Code with commands, MCP servers, and bundled skills. It is the marketplace layer for an agent already in this catalog, not a separate product.

name: Claudex-Loop
about: Claude Code skill that hardens a plan with Codex as adversary
description: Claudex-Loop is a Claude Code skill for four-phase plan hardening: recon, interrogation, Codex adversarial review, then a split where the model that built the work does not grade it. Search claude codex review loop or adversarial plan skill.

name: CleanMyKeyboard
about: Locks the Mac keyboard so you can wipe it without typing junk
description: CleanMyKeyboard disables key input while you clean the keyboard, then unlocks with a gesture or shortcut. Search clean keyboard mac or disable keys to wipe.

name: Cleanup.pictures
about: AI tool that removes unwanted objects or people from photos
description: Cleanup.pictures uses AI to let users paint over unwanted objects, people, text, or watermarks in a photo and automatically fills in the background naturally. It pairs well with background-removal tools for full photo cleanup without needing Photoshop skills.

name: ClickUp
about: All-in-one workspace for tasks, docs, chat, and AI agents
description: ClickUp is a workspace that combines projects, docs, chat, whiteboards, and AI agents in one product, aiming to replace a pile of separate tools. Where Asana stays focused on work tracking, ClickUp is the kitchen-sink suite.

name: Cline
about: Open-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains, and CLI
description: Cline is an autonomous coding agent you run as an IDE extension, SDK, or CLI with your own model keys. It is the open VS Code-native counterpart to Cursor for people who want agent edits inside an editor they already use.

name: Colibri
about: Pure-C inference engine that streams huge MoE models from disk
description: Colibri runs very large mixture-of-experts models on consumer hardware by streaming weights from disk instead of loading everything into RAM. It targets people who want local inference beyond what a typical Ollama pull can fit in memory.

name: Colorize.cc
about: AI colorizes black and white photos automatically
description: Colorize.cc uses AI to add realistic color to black-and-white photos automatically, useful for restoring old family photos or historical images. It's a focused single-purpose tool alongside the rest of the photo-editing cluster.

name: ComfyUI
about: Local node-based UI for diffusion image and video models
description: ComfyUI is a graph/node interface for running Stable Diffusion and other generative models locally, with full control over pipelines. Artists and researchers use it when they need a modular workbench instead of a hosted one-click generator.

name: Connected Papers
about: Visual graph of academic papers related by citation
description: Connected Papers builds a visual graph of academic papers connected by shared citations, helping researchers discover related work and trace a field's key papers from a single starting point. It's popular among students and academics for literature review and research discovery.

name: Core Framework
about: Visual CSS and design-token builder for web, WordPress, and Figma
description: Core Framework is a design-system builder that exports CSS variables and tokens into web projects, WordPress themes, and Figma workflows. It targets designers who want a structured token pipeline instead of one-off style tweaks in Canva or Penpot alone.

name: Crawl4AI
about: LLM-friendly web crawler that outputs markdown and JSON
description: Crawl4AI fetches and cleans web pages into markdown or structured JSON tuned for RAG pipelines and agents. It ships with CLI and Docker surfaces so teams can run it as a crawl service instead of hand-rolling BeautifulSoup scrapers.

name: Cumora
about: Team chat where AI agents are first-class participants
description: Cumora is team chat software that treats AI agents as peers in channels, not bolt-on bots. It competes in the same human-plus-agent workspace lane as Buzz for teams self-hosting collaboration with embedded agents.

name: Curbox
about: Android app and site blocker with focus modes and overlays
description: Curbox blocks or greys out distracting apps and page regions, with schedules, unlock friction, and usage stats. Search android app blocker, focus mode, or hide youtube feed.

name: Cursor
about: AI-native code editor with inline autocomplete and repo-wide agents
description: Cursor is an AI-native code editor (a VS Code fork) with tab autocomplete, multi-file agents, and optional cloud agents that build and demo features in parallel. It is the IDE-shaped counterpart to terminal coding agents like Claude Code, and it runs on a free Hobby tier with paid upgrades for heavier agent use.

name: DeepSec
about: Agent-powered vulnerability scanner for large codebases
description: DeepSec from Vercel Labs uses coding agents to hunt security issues across big repositories, going deeper than a single-file linter pass. Security-minded teams run it when they want AI-assisted review that can follow call chains and config across a monorepo.

name: DeepSeek Harness
about: Plugin-based coding-agent runtime from DeepSeek
description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is an open agent runtime where every capability is a plugin. Developers use it to run coding agents with a growing plugin ecosystem rather than a fixed toolbelt, closer to an extensible host than a single-vendor CLI.

name: DeepTutor
about: Agent-native personalized AI tutor and learning workspace
description: DeepTutor from HKUDS is an AI learning workspace that adapts explanations, drills, and study plans around what you are trying to learn. It targets students and lifelong learners who want a tutor-shaped agent rather than a generic chat box.

name: Descript
about: AI video and podcast editor that edits like a doc
description: Descript transcribes recordings so you edit video and podcasts by editing text, with overdub and filler-word removal. Search podcast editor or edit video as text and this is the product; WhisperX is the local transcription engine already in the catalog.

name: designer-skills
about: Agent skills for design work in Claude and Cursor
description: designer-skills collects prompts and procedures for design-centric agent tasks like critique, layout iteration, and asset handoff. It is a general-purpose design skill bundle for people who live in Claude Code or Cursor all day.

name: DeskMinder
about: Sticky reminders that live on the Mac desktop
description: DeskMinder pins reminders and notes to the desktop instead of burying them in a list app. Search desktop sticky notes mac or desktop reminders.

name: dgit
about: Git forge that runs on Cloudflare Durable Objects
description: dgit is an experimental git hosting layer built on Cloudflare Durable Objects, aiming for cheap, edge-local repos without a traditional forge VM. Developers try it as infrastructure curiosity when exploring serverless git rather than as a GitHub replacement for teams.

name: Diagram Design
about: Agent skill for editorial HTML+SVG diagrams without Mermaid slop
description: Diagram Design is a Claude Code, Codex, and Pi skill that renders 39 diagram types as self-contained HTML and SVG with an editorial aesthetic. Install it when you want presentation-quality architecture and flow diagrams from an agent instead of default Mermaid exports.

name: DishGen
about: AI generates a novel recipe from ingredients or a craving
description: DishGen generates original recipes on demand from a list of ingredients, a cuisine, or a described craving, rather than matching against an existing recipe database like Supercook does. It's aimed at people wanting inspiration beyond what's already been written down.

name: Dockside
about: File shelf that sits beside the Mac Dock
description: Dockside is a staging shelf next to the Dock for recent downloads, screenshots, and drag-and-drop files. Search mac dock shelf or file staging mac.

name: Documenso
about: Open-source e-signature platform, a DocuSign alternative
description: Documenso lets you upload, sign, and send documents for e-signature, with a self-hostable open-source backend as an alternative to closed SaaS tools like DocuSign.

name: draw.io
about: Free browser-based diagramming and flowchart tool
description: draw.io (also known as diagrams.net) is a free, open-source diagramming tool for creating flowcharts, org charts, network diagrams, and UML, with integrations for Google Drive, Confluence, and local file storage. It's a staple for developers and technical writers documenting systems.

name: Droid-ify
about: Clean F-Droid client for installing open-source Android apps
description: Droid-ify is a material F-Droid client for browsing and updating FOSS Android apps without the stock client's clutter. It is software discovery on Android in the same job as Ninite on Windows.

name: DSPy
about: Stanford framework for programming LLM pipelines instead of prompting
description: DSPy from Stanford treats prompts and few-shot examples as optimizable programs rather than hand-written strings. Researchers and engineers use it to compile reliable LLM pipelines with automatic tuning instead of endless prompt tweaking.

name: Dub
about: Open-source link shortener with analytics, a Bitly alternative
description: Dub is an open-source link management platform offering short links, click analytics, and branded domains, positioned as a modern alternative to Bitly.

name: EarthCam
about: Live public webcams from locations around the world
description: EarthCam aggregates live public webcam feeds from tourist landmarks, cities, and scenic locations globally, letting anyone watch a live view of places in real time. It's used for virtual tourism, event viewing, and casual browsing.

name: ElevenLabs
about: AI voice generation and cloning, text-to-speech
description: ElevenLabs generates highly realistic AI voices from text and can clone specific voices from short audio samples, supporting multiple languages and emotional tones. It's widely used for audiobooks, video narration, dubbing, and voice-based product features.

name: Elicit
about: AI research assistant that searches papers and extracts cited findings
description: Elicit searches a corpus of over a hundred million academic papers, pulls findings into structured tables, and generates research reports with sentence-level citations. Unlike Connected Papers' citation graph or Perplexity's open-web answers, it stays scoped to the scientific literature and is built for systematic reviews and evidence synthesis.

name: Emil Kowalski Skills
about: Flagship Claude/Cursor skill pack for UI animation and design engineering
description: Emil Kowalski's skills teach agents how to implement polished motion, layout, and interaction details the way a design engineer would. It is one of the most-installed design-eng skill packs for Claude Code and Cursor users shipping production UI.

name: Excalidraw
about: Hand-drawn style whiteboard and diagramming tool
description: Excalidraw is an open-source virtual whiteboard for sketching diagrams, wireframes, and ideas with a distinctive hand-drawn visual style. It's popular for quick collaborative brainstorming and technical sketches where a formal diagramming tool feels too rigid.

name: FineTune
about: Open-source macOS menu bar app for per-app volume control and audio routing
description: FineTune provides independent per-application volume sliders, volume boosting up to 4x, multi-device audio routing, and a 10-band equalizer directly from the macOS menu bar. It serves as a free, open-source alternative to SoundSource for users wanting granular control over individual app audio streams.

name: FlightRadar24
about: Real-time global flight tracking map
description: FlightRadar24 tracks tens of thousands of aircraft in real time on an interactive world map, showing flight paths, altitude, speed, and aircraft details sourced from ADS-B receivers worldwide. It's used by travelers, aviation enthusiasts, and anyone tracking a specific flight.

name: FluidVoice
about: Local voice dictation tool for hands-free text input
description: FluidVoice is a voice dictation app that transcribes speech to text locally on-device, letting users dictate into any app without sending audio to the cloud.

name: Fold Switcher
about: Force foldable Android devices into specific fold states
description: Fold Switcher switches a foldable phone between folded, unfolded, and other display states on demand. Search foldable android emulator state or force unfold when debugging or using desktop-style apps on a foldable.

name: Folder Scope
about: Quick Look extension to preview folder hierarchies and compressed archives in Finder
description: Folder Scope integrates with macOS Quick Look to display the contents of folders and compressed archives like ZIP, RAR, 7Z, and TAR right inside Finder using the spacebar. It eliminates the need to extract archives or open new windows just to inspect directory trees and file listings.

name: Forel
about: Open-source folder automation, a Hazel alternative
description: Forel watches folders and runs rules on new files — sort, rename, convert — on-device. It is the open-source stand-in for Hazel when you want file automation without a paid license.

name: FreeLLMAPI
about: Proxy that aggregates free-tier LLM providers behind one API
description: FreeLLMAPI routes requests across multiple providers' free tiers through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint for personal experimentation. It overlaps LiteLLM but optimizes for zero-cost tinkering, with the tradeoff that free-tier ToS limits still apply upstream.

name: FutureMe
about: Write an email to yourself, delivered on a future date you choose
description: FutureMe lets users write a letter or email addressed to their future self, scheduled for delivery on a chosen future date, from months to years ahead. It's used for goal-setting, reflection, and personal time-capsule style journaling.

name: Futurepedia
about: Directory of AI tools, catalogued and reviewed
description: Futurepedia is a directory site cataloging and reviewing new AI tools across categories like writing, image, video, and productivity. It functions like AlternativeTo but scoped specifically to the fast-moving AI tools space.

name: garden-skills
about: Collection of Claude Code and agent skills
description: garden-skills is a curated repo of installable agent skills for Claude Code and compatible assistants. It functions as a small skill garden you clone or add rather than a single-purpose prompt file.

name: GeoSpy
about: AI tool that geolocates photos from visual clues
description: GeoSpy uses AI to analyze visual clues in a photograph — landscape, architecture, signage — and estimate where it was taken. It's used in OSINT investigations, journalism verification, and security research, and carries the usual dual-use privacy considerations of geolocation tools.

name: Ghostty
about: Fast, native GPU terminal emulator
description: Ghostty is a GPU-accelerated terminal from Mitchell Hashimoto that aims to be fast and native on macOS and Linux. Developers install it as a modern terminal that still behaves like a well-mannered OS citizen.

name: Gling
about: AI editor that cuts silences, filler words, and bad takes from talking-head video
description: Gling transcribes a recording, auto-removes silences, filler words, and bad takes, and exports to MP4 or as XML into Final Cut, Premiere, and DaVinci Resolve. Opus Clip is for turning long videos into short-form clips; Gling is for cleaning the long-form cut.

name: Go Modern Guidelines
about: JetBrains guidelines so coding agents write modern Go
description: Go Modern Guidelines is a JetBrains pack that teaches AI coding agents current Go style, APIs, and idioms. Drop it into an agent project when you want generated Go to match modern practice instead of outdated tutorials.

name: God's Eye View
about: Browser globe that shows live open-source satellite and geo intel
description: God's Eye View is a photorealistic 3D globe fed with real open spatial data — a spy-satellite simulator that is not fake. It sits next to FlightRadar24 and Windy as a browsable geo toy that is also a real OSINT viewer.

name: Google AI Studio
about: Web playground for Gemini and other Google models, with an API key built in
description: Google AI Studio is the browser playground for Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana, and related Google models — prompt, compare outputs, and mint an API key without standing up Cloud infrastructure. It is the developer-facing counterpart to NotebookLM: experiment with models here, ground answers in your own documents there.

name: Google Lens
about: Point your camera at anything to search, translate, or identify it
description: Google Lens uses visual search to identify objects, plants, and landmarks, extract and translate text, and find shopping matches directly from a photo or camera view. It's built into Google's app and Chrome rather than a standalone site, but its web entry point makes it usable from any browser.

name: Grammarly
about: Cloud grammar, spelling, and tone checker
description: Grammarly checks grammar, spelling, and tone in the browser, desktop apps, and editors. It is the mainstream writing assistant; Harper is the offline open-source alternative already listed.

name: GrandPerspective
about: Mac disk-usage treemap to find what is eating space
description: GrandPerspective draws a treemap of files and folders so large space hogs jump out visually. Search disk usage Mac or storage treemap; Mole handles cleanup and Rascal includes a treemap inside a file manager.

name: Halcyon Video
about: Turns a Jellyfin library into a walkable 90s video store
description: Halcyon Video is a novelty front-end that renders your Jellyfin movie collection as a nostalgic Blockbuster-style store you can wander through. It is entertainment software for media hoarders, in the same spirit as Radiooooo or The Useless Web.

name: Harness Engineering
about: Playbooks and patterns for shaping effective agent environments
description: Harness Engineering is a documentation anthology on how to design repositories, tools, and guardrails so coding agents succeed reliably. It is reference material for agent builders, not a runnable app — closer to a curated guide than a CLI.

name: Harper
about: Offline, privacy-first grammar checker
description: Harper is a free, open-source grammar checker from Automattic that runs on-device. Writers and developers use it when they want grammar help without sending drafts to Grammarly's cloud.

name: Have I Been Pwned
about: Checks if your email or password appeared in known data breaches
description: Have I Been Pwned lets users check whether their email address or password has appeared in a known data breach, aggregating breach data from thousands of incidents. It's an essential first step for assessing personal security exposure and pairs naturally with password managers.

name: Hemingway Editor
about: Writing tool that flags complex sentences and readability issues
description: Hemingway Editor analyzes text and highlights overly complex sentences, passive voice, adverb overuse, and readability grade level, helping writers produce clearer, punchier prose. It's popular with bloggers, marketers, and students editing drafts.

name: Herdr
about: Runtime that local coding agents live on
description: Herdr is the host layer coding agents run on: sessions, terminals, and orchestration rather than another IDE or model CLI. Use it when you want Claude Code, Codex, and similar agents sharing one runtime instead of scattered processes.

name: Hindsight
about: Agent skill that saves durable process lessons from a session
description: Hindsight reviews a coding-agent session and writes only reusable process lessons into persistent memory, skipping one-off trivia. Search agent session memory skill or coding assistant retrospect.

name: Holehe
about: OSINT CLI that checks if an email is registered on 120+ sites
description: Holehe is a Python CLI that tests whether an email address has accounts on hundreds of websites without alerting the target. Investigators pair it with OSINT Framework and Have I Been Pwned when mapping someone's online footprint from an email alone.

name: Homebrew
about: Package manager for macOS and Linux
description: Homebrew installs command-line tools and desktop apps from the terminal with a single brew command. It is the de facto package manager on Mac, and the closest equivalent to Ninite for Unix machines that live in a shell.

name: How a Car Works
about: Illustrated encyclopedia explaining how every car system works
description: How a Car Works is an illustrated online guide breaking down engines, transmissions, brakes, electrics, and every other major car system into clear diagrams and plain-language explanations. It's aimed at owners, students, and hobbyists who want to actually understand their vehicle rather than just look up a repair step.

name: HQBase
about: Shared team inbox that runs on your Cloudflare account
description: HQBase deploys a shared email inbox on infrastructure you control through Cloudflare, so small teams can collaborate on support or ops mail without Google Workspace. It is early but fills a self-hosted email gap most catalogs skip.

name: Hyperkey
about: Turns Caps Lock into a Hyper modifier key on Mac
description: Hyperkey remaps Caps Lock (or another modifier) into the Hyper key — Control, Option, Command, and Shift together. Power users bind extra shortcuts to it without fighting the built-in modifier set.

name: iLovePDF
about: PDF toolkit for merging, splitting, compressing, and converting
description: iLovePDF offers a focused set of PDF tools — merge, split, compress, convert to/from Word or images, and more — through a simple browser interface. It's a specialist alternative to broader multi-format sites like TinyWow, favored for PDF-specific workflows.

name: Imagine CLI
about: Go CLI for image generation across Gemini, Vertex, and OpenAI
description: Imagine CLI is a single-binary command-line tool that generates and edits images through Gemini, Vertex AI, or OpenAI from a YAML config file. It suits developers who want scriptable image gen without opening Google AI Studio or a web UI.

name: img2threejs
about: Agent skill that turns an image into procedural Three.js code
description: img2threejs is an agent skill that recreates reference images as procedural Three.js scenes instead of flat textures. Frontend developers install it when they want interactive 3D hero graphics generated inside Claude Code or similar agents.

name: Immich
about: Self-hosted photo and video backup, a Google Photos alternative
description: Immich is an open-source, self-hosted platform for backing up and managing photos and videos from phones and computers, with mobile apps, facial recognition, and timeline browsing similar to Google Photos.

name: ImportYeti
about: Searches US customs records to find suppliers and importers by product
description: ImportYeti searches US customs bills of lading to reveal which companies import specific products and who their suppliers are. It's used for supply chain research, competitor analysis, and sourcing new manufacturers.

name: InstallerX Revived
about: Expressive Android package installer, the live InstallerX tree
description: InstallerX Revived is the maintained continuation of InstallerX for installing APKs, APKS, and related formats with a modern UI, including Shizuku/root hooks. The original InstallerX repo is gone; this is the project people actually ship.

name: Instructor
about: Python library for structured LLM outputs via Pydantic schemas
description: Instructor wraps LLM calls so responses validate against Pydantic models instead of loose JSON blobs. It is the go-to library when you need typed, retry-aware structured generation in Python agents and APIs.

name: iPiccy
about: Free browser photo editor with filters, effects, and collage tools
description: iPiccy is a free browser-based photo editor covering filters, retouching, effects, and collage-making in a simple, casual interface. It's aimed at quick everyday photo edits rather than the deeper pro-level editing Photopea offers.

name: Itsycal
about: Tiny Mac menu-bar calendar with Calendar.app events
description: Itsycal is a small menu-bar calendar that shows the month and your Mac Calendar events. Search menu bar calendar Mac.

name: Jakub Krehel Skills
about: Claude skills focused on UI polish and visual refinement
description: Jakub Krehel Skills encodes subtle UI polish patterns — shadows, borders, states, and micro-layout — for agents implementing interfaces. Frontend developers install it when generated UI needs to look finished, not bootstrapped.

name: Jan
about: Desktop ChatGPT alternative that runs locally
description: Jan is an open-source desktop app for chatting with local or cloud models, aimed at people who want a ChatGPT-style UI without a hosted account. It complements Open WebUI: native app versus self-hosted web.

name: JustWatch
about: Search where to stream a movie or show across all platforms
description: JustWatch aggregates streaming availability across Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, and dozens of other platforms, letting users search a title and instantly see where it's available to stream, rent, or buy. It's the go-to tool for avoiding subscription-hopping guesswork.

name: Keyviz
about: Real-time keystroke and mouse action visualizer for presentations and screencasts
description: Keyviz visualizes keyboard shortcuts and mouse clicks on-screen in real time, making it easy for viewers to follow along during presentations, tutorials, and screen recordings. It features customizable keycap styles, animations, mouse indicators, and hotkey filtering to show only relevant combinations.

name: Khoj
about: Self-hosted AI second brain over your documents and notes
description: Khoj indexes your files and notes so you can chat with your own knowledge base, optionally augmented with web search. It is a self-hostable personal research assistant in the same lane as NotebookLM, aimed at people who want their data on their own server.

name: Koe
about: Prompt-to-video generator with a music-video workflow
description: Koe generates videos from a text prompt or script, with a music-video mode that pairs well with a generated track. Compared with Runway's broader creative suite, it is a more focused prompt-to-video tool with a free starting plan.

name: Kofe Flow
about: Private menu-bar Pomodoro timer for Mac
description: Kofe Flow is a menu-bar Pomodoro and focus timer. Search pomodoro mac menu bar or focus timer mac.

name: landing-page-design
about: Agent skills for generating landing-page design
description: landing-page-design is a skill pack focused on marketing-site layout, typography, and component choices when agents build landing pages. Designers install it to keep codegen output closer to a deliberate marketing design system.

name: Langfuse
about: Open-source LLM observability and tracing you can self-host
description: Langfuse records traces, costs, and quality metrics for LLM applications so teams can debug prompts and monitor production agents. It is the open-source alternative to hosted LLM ops dashboards, with a UI teams actually run day to day.

name: Launchy
about: Radial app launcher and window switcher for macOS
description: Launchy displays a radial menu around the mouse cursor or screen center for quick launching and switching between apps, files, and folders. It replaces Command-Tab cycling and Dock hunting with customizable circular palettes, keyboard navigation, and iCloud sync.

name: Library Genesis (LibGen)
about: Shadow library offering free downloads of books and papers
description: Library Genesis is a shadow library providing free access to millions of books, academic papers, and articles, many of which are under copyright. Its legality varies by jurisdiction and it operates in a legal gray area regarding copyright infringement — include and use with that risk understood.

name: LibreTranslate
about: Self-hosted machine translation API with no cloud dependency
description: LibreTranslate is an open-source translation server you can run locally or on your own infrastructure, exposing a simple REST API for text translation. It is for teams that need translation without sending content to Google or DeepL.

name: ListMonk
about: Self-hosted newsletter and mailing list manager
description: ListMonk is a high-performance, self-hostable newsletter and bulk mailing list manager, used as an open-source alternative to hosted email marketing platforms like Mailchimp.

name: LiteLLM
about: OpenAI-compatible gateway to 100+ LLM providers with a proxy UI
description: LiteLLM exposes one OpenAI-shaped API in front of Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, and dozens of other providers, with optional routing, budgets, and a management UI. Teams deploy it as the central LLM gateway instead of hard-coding every vendor SDK.

name: LittleSis.org
about: Crowd-sourced database mapping relationships between powerful people and organizations
description: LittleSis is a free, crowd-sourced database that maps connections between politicians, executives, corporations, and organizations, exposing relationships not disclosed in official records. It's a power-mapping and investigative research tool used by journalists and researchers.

name: Loom
about: Async video messages and screen recordings
description: Loom records the screen, camera, and mic into a shareable link for async updates. Search screen recording or video messages and this is the hosted default; Cap is the open-source alternative already in the catalog.

name: Loop
about: Radial window manager for macOS
description: Loop is a keyboard-driven Mac window manager with a radial menu for snapping and moving windows. It fills the window-management gap on a catalog that had none.

name: Lumina
about: Local-first agentic desktop companion with personas
description: Lumina is a desktop companion app that runs agents locally with switchable personas for different tasks. It is a smaller entrant in the local agent desktop lane for people experimenting beyond browser chat UIs.

name: Maccy
about: Lightweight clipboard history for Mac
description: Maccy keeps a searchable history of everything you copy and pastes it back with a shortcut. It is the small, open-source clipboard manager Mac users install when the system clipboard is not enough.

name: macOS Harness
about: Agent skill with primitives for controlling a Mac from an LLM
description: macOS Harness exposes safe, composable macOS automation primitives so agents can click, type, and navigate the desktop. It is for builders wiring computer-use agents on Apple hardware rather than end users running a standalone app.

name: MapCrunch
about: Teleports you to a random Google Street View location
description: MapCrunch drops you into a random spot on Google Street View anywhere in the world, letting you explore streets, landscapes, and towns you'd never otherwise stumble on. It's a virtual-travel novelty tool often used for casual exploration or as a geo-guessing game.

name: Marker
about: Local PDF and document converter to clean markdown or JSON
description: Marker converts PDFs, slides, and scans into high-quality markdown, JSON, or HTML using local models tuned for layout preservation. It is popular in RAG and research workflows where you need structured text from messy documents without a cloud upload step.

name: Memhogs
about: CLI that rolls helper processes up so you see which app owns RAM
description: Memhogs is a zero-dependency Go CLI for macOS and Linux that attributes memory to the app that owns helper and child processes. Search which app is using memory or memory hogs cli; NeoHtop is the GUI process monitor.

name: Meng To Skills
about: Design-oriented Claude skills from Meng To
description: Meng To Skills packages the Design+Code author's UI craft as agent skills for typography, spacing, and iOS-style polish. It is for designers who already follow Meng To's work and want agents to mirror that visual language.

name: Microsoft Math Solver
about: Photo or type a math problem, get a free step-by-step solution
description: Microsoft Math Solver reads a handwritten, typed, or photographed math problem and returns a free step-by-step solution with explanations, covering algebra through calculus. Its step-by-step tutoring focus is free where WolframAlpha paywalls that depth, making it a strong companion for students.

name: Midjourney
about: Hosted AI image generation with a distinctive aesthetic
description: Midjourney generates images from text prompts, known for a painterly look and an iterative web workflow. It is the name most people search for in AI image generation; ComfyUI is the local node-based counterpart already in the catalog.

name: MiniMind
about: Train a tiny LLM from scratch in about two hours
description: MiniMind is a teaching codebase for training a ~64M-parameter language model from scratch on a single machine. Search train llm from scratch or small llm tutorial.

name: Minto Pyramid Skill
about: Agent skill that rewrites prose in Barbara Minto's pyramid style
description: This skill teaches coding agents to structure memos and emails answer-first with grouped supporting reasons, following the Minto Pyramid Principle. Consultants and operators install it to stop agents from burying the lede in narrative drafts.

name: ModelDeck
about: Mac menu bar meters for Claude Code and Codex rate limits
description: ModelDeck shows percent-left and reset countdowns for Claude Code and Codex CLI accounts in the menu bar. Search claude code usage or codex rate limit meter; CC-Switch is the provider-switcher already listed.

name: Modular
about: Mojo language and MAX inference platform from Modular
description: Modular is the company behind Mojo, a Python-superset systems language for AI kernels, and MAX, its inference engine stack. It is developer infrastructure for people building high-performance model runtimes, not an end-user chat app.

name: Mole
about: Open-source Mac cleaner, uninstaller, and disk analyzer
description: Mole is a free Mac maintenance tool for uninstalling apps, clearing junk, and inspecting disk use, with both a CLI and a native app. It is the CleanMyMac-shaped option that stays local and open-source.

name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
about: Auto-generates short videos from a topic prompt
description: MoneyPrinterTurbo chains scripting, voice, footage, and editing steps to produce short-form videos from a single topic prompt. It sits in the automated video lane next to Runway and Opus Clip for creators who want a self-hosted pipeline rather than a studio UI.

name: Morph
about: Fast Apply API that merges coding-agent edits into files
description: Morph is a model API for coding agents, best known for Fast Apply: a small model that merges lazy edit snippets into full files at high speed. Agent and IDE builders use it instead of brittle search-replace or full-file rewrites.

name: MyHeritage Deep Nostalgia
about: AI animates old still photos with subtle lifelike movement
description: Deep Nostalgia, a MyHeritage feature, uses AI to animate a still photo with subtle head movement, blinking, and smiling, most often used to bring old family photos of relatives to life. It's built around genealogy and nostalgia rather than general-purpose photo editing.

name: MyNoise.net
about: Customizable ambient and background noise generator
description: MyNoise.net offers a large library of finely tunable ambient soundscapes — rain, white noise, nature sounds — with detailed sliders to shape the exact sound profile. It's used for focus, relaxation, sleep, and masking distracting background noise.

name: n8n
about: Open-source workflow automation you can self-host
description: n8n is an open-source workflow automation tool with a node-based editor, optional JavaScript or Python in any step, and a self-hosted option so data stays on your infrastructure. It is the Zapier alternative for technical teams who want the visual builder without sending every integration through a third-party cloud.

name: Napkin AI
about: Turns pasted text into editable diagrams, flowcharts, and infographics
description: Napkin AI generates diagrams, flowcharts, mind maps, and infographics from writing you paste or import, then lets you restyle and export to PPT, PNG, PDF, or SVG. Where draw.io and Excalidraw start from a blank canvas, Napkin builds the first visual from the text itself.

name: nautilus_trader
about: Production-grade Rust algo-trading engine with Python strategies
description: nautilus_trader is a high-performance algorithmic trading platform with a Rust core and Python strategy layer for backtesting and live execution. Quant developers use it when they need serious event-driven trading infrastructure rather than notebook prototypes.

name: Needle
about: Tiny on-device tool-calling model shipped as a ~14MB binary
description: Needle is a 45M-parameter model packaged as a small binary that can call tools on edge hardware without cloud round-trips. It is a research-flavored product for developers experimenting with local agent loops on constrained devices.

name: NeoHtop
about: Modern desktop process monitor, an htop with a real UI
description: NeoHtop is a fast, cross-platform system monitor built with Rust and Tauri. It is for people who want Activity Monitor / htop in a cleaner desktop UI instead of a terminal dashboard.

name: Network Switch
about: One-tap 4G/5G network switching on Android
description: Network Switch flips between network generations (4G/5G) without digging through SIM settings. Search switch 5g android or force lte.

name: Ninite
about: Pick apps, get one clean installer, no bloatware or toolbars
description: Ninite generates a single installer for a batch of chosen apps, installing them silently in the background without extra toolbars, bundled bloatware, or browser hijackers. It's a fast way to set up a fresh Windows machine or keep existing software updated with minimal manual work.

name: NorthCinder
about: Shopping MCP that compares products and waits for approval before buying
description: NorthCinder is a Model Context Protocol server that lets agents research products, compare options, and pause for human approval before any purchase executes. Shoppers install it when they want agent-assisted buying with an explicit checkout gate.

name: NotebookLM
about: Upload your documents, get an AI notebook with summaries, Q&A, and audio overviews
description: NotebookLM is Google's AI research assistant that grounds its answers entirely in documents you upload, generating summaries, answering questions, and producing an audio-overview "podcast" discussing your sources. Unlike Perplexity's open web search, it stays scoped to exactly what you feed it, making it well-suited for research, study, and document synthesis.

name: Notion
about: All-in-one workspace for notes, wikis, and databases
description: Notion combines documents, wikis, project boards, and databases in one workspace used by individuals and teams. Search for notes, knowledge bases, or a Notion-style wiki and this is the default hit, with AppFlowy and AFFiNE as open alternatives.

name: NUKEMAP
about: Simulates nuclear detonation blast effects on any map location
description: NUKEMAP lets users simulate the blast radius, fallout, and casualty estimates of a nuclear detonation at any chosen location on a real map, using historical and modern weapon yields. It's an educational visualization tool built for public understanding of nuclear weapons effects, not a how-to resource.

name: Ollama
about: Local LLM runtime with a Docker-like CLI and local API
description: Ollama lets you pull and run open-weight language models on your own machine through a simple CLI and a local HTTP API. It is the standard way developers run Llama, Mistral, and similar models offline without wiring up raw inference servers.

name: Omarchy
about: DHH/Basecamp opinionated Arch + Hyprland Linux desktop distro
description: Omarchy is a curated Arch Linux setup from 37signals with Hyprland, a focused app set, and strong defaults for developers who want a polished tiling desktop without assembling dotfiles from scratch. It is a full OS flavor, not a single utility.

name: OMFGDOGS
about: A spinning dog gif and nothing else, internet-culture novelty relic
description: OMFGDOGS is a single-page novelty site from early internet meme culture — a spinning dog gif set to music, with zero other function. It exists purely as a nostalgic, absurdist novelty in the same vein as The Useless Web.

name: OmniRoute
about: Free MIT gateway to hundreds of LLM providers, including free tiers
description: OmniRoute is a single endpoint over 300+ providers and 1000+ models, with a large free-model pool, aimed at Claude Code, Cline, Codex, and Cursor. Search free claude code models or multi-provider llm gateway; LiteLLM remains the general proxy already listed.

name: Open Interpreter
about: Terminal coding agent that runs code locally on your machine
description: Open Interpreter was an early local computer-use agent: a CLI that executes Python, shell, and browser actions on your machine from natural language. It remains a reference implementation for running models with real system access instead of chat-only replies.

name: Open SEO
about: Open-source alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs
description: Open SEO is an open toolkit for keyword research, backlink analysis, and Search Console-style workflows, including agent/MCP hooks. Marketers and developers use it when they want SEO suite features without a Semrush subscription.

name: Open WebUI
about: Self-hosted ChatGPT-style UI for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs
description: Open WebUI is a browser-based chat interface you self-host on top of Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It gives local models a polished multi-user UI with history, RAG hooks, and admin controls instead of curling a raw API.

name: OpenAI Codex
about: OpenAI's open-source terminal coding agent (Apache 2.0)
description: OpenAI Codex is Anthropic Claude Code's counterpart from OpenAI: an open-source CLI agent that reads repos, edits files, runs commands, and ships changes. The client is free to use; model access goes through your OpenAI subscription or API key.

name: OpenClaude
about: Open-source Claude Code-shaped agent that runs anywhere
description: OpenClaude is an open coding agent meant to run on your machine with whatever models you plug in. It is the OSS counterpart to Claude Code for people who want that CLI workflow without being locked to Anthropic.

name: OpenCorporates
about: Largest open database of company and corporate registry data
description: OpenCorporates aggregates official company registry data from jurisdictions worldwide into a single searchable open database, covering millions of legal entities. It's used for due diligence, corporate research, and investigative journalism.

name: OpenHands
about: Open-source platform for AI software-engineering agents
description: OpenHands is a self-hostable agent platform with GUI, CLI, and SDK surfaces for letting models read repos, run commands, and open pull requests. It is the open infrastructure play in the coding-agent space, distinct from closed apps like Cursor.

name: OpenLogi
about: Native local-first Logitech Options+ alternative, no account required
description: OpenLogi is a Rust desktop app that configures Logitech mice and keyboards over HID++ without Logitech's cloud account or Options+ bloat. It appeals to privacy-minded users who want full device control locally on macOS and Linux.

name: OpenMAIC
about: One-click multi-agent interactive classroom
description: OpenMAIC (Open Multi-Agent Interactive Classroom) spins up an immersive multi-agent learning session in the browser. Students and teachers use it when they want several AI tutors in one room rather than a single chatbot.

name: OpenMontage
about: Open-source agentic video production studio
description: OpenMontage is an agentic video production system with pipelines, tools, and skill files that turn a coding assistant into a video studio. Creators use it for scripted, multi-step generation rather than a single text-to-video button.

name: OpenViking
about: Context database that treats agent memory and skills as a filesystem
description: OpenViking from Volcengine is an agent context store that mounts memories, tools, and skills like files so agents can browse and update long-term state. It targets builders who want structured agent memory beyond stuffing everything into a prompt window.

name: OpnForm
about: Open-source form builder, a Typeform alternative
description: OpnForm is a self-hostable form builder for surveys, waitlists, and intake flows. Use the cloud or run it yourself when you want Typeform-style forms without the SaaS tax.

name: Opus Clip
about: AI tool that auto-clips long videos into short-form highlights
description: Opus Clip uses AI to analyze long-form video and automatically generate short, highlight-worthy clips optimized for platforms like TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. It's built for content creators who want to repurpose long content without manual editing.

name: Orca
about: Agent IDE for running coding agents in parallel worktrees
description: Orca is an agent development environment for running Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents side by side, each in its own worktree, with terminals, diffs, and a browser in one app. It ships on desktop, mobile, and VPS so you can drive a fleet of agents from your own subscriptions.

name: OSINT Framework
about: Directory of OSINT tools and resources organized by category
description: OSINT Framework is a curated directory linking out to hundreds of open-source intelligence tools and resources, organized into a browsable category tree covering usernames, emails, social media, geolocation, and more. It's a starting point for security researchers and investigators mapping what tools exist for a given task.

name: Otter.ai
about: AI meeting notetaker that transcribes, summarizes, and captures action items
description: Otter.ai joins or records meetings, produces live transcripts with speaker labels, and turns the conversation into summaries and action items you can search later. It is a meeting-knowledge tool, not a general voice generator like ElevenLabs.

name: Outlines
about: Constrained and structured generation library for LLMs
description: Outlines forces language models to emit outputs that match grammars, regexes, or JSON schemas at decode time. Teams pair it with local or API models when free-form prompting is too flaky for production extraction and classification.

name: Outpost
about: Hotkey launcher for dropping files onto apps, folders, and actions
description: Outpost summons a palette at the cursor so you can drag files onto pinned apps, folders, or shortcuts without hunting Finder windows. Search mac file launcher or drag-and-drop shelf.

name: Oyster
about: Hotel reviews backed by unbiased photos from paid on-site inspectors
description: Oyster sends professional photographers and writers to hotels to shoot unretouched photos and write independent reviews, countering the curated marketing photos hotels typically publish themselves. It's used by travelers who want an honest look at a property before booking.

name: PairDrop
about: Browser-to-browser local file transfer, no cloud upload
description: PairDrop lets devices on the same local network transfer files directly browser-to-browser without uploading to any cloud service, similar to AirDrop but working across Windows, Android, Linux, and more. It's open source, requires no signup, and keeps transfers private since data never leaves the local network.

name: PCPartPicker
about: Build a PC part list with automatic compatibility checks and price comparison
description: PCPartPicker lets you assemble a custom PC build from a component database that flags compatibility issues — socket mismatches, wattage shortfalls, clearance conflicts — and compares live prices across retailers. It's the standard tool for both first-time builders and enthusiasts planning a rig.

name: PDFescape
about: Browser-based PDF editor for filling forms and annotating documents
description: PDFescape lets you edit, annotate, and fill forms directly on a PDF in the browser, without needing Acrobat. Its focus on in-place editing and form-filling sets it apart from convert/merge/split-oriented tools like iLovePDF.

name: Penpot
about: Open-source design and prototyping tool, a Figma alternative
description: Penpot is a self-hostable, browser-based design and prototyping tool built on open web standards, used by designers and developers as an open-source alternative to Figma.

name: Perplexica
about: Self-hosted Perplexity-style answer engine with citations
description: Perplexica (rebranding to Vane) is a self-hostable AI search app that answers questions with cited sources, similar to Perplexity but on your own hardware. It fits the same self-hosted-alternative pattern as Immich or AppFlowy for people who want answer engines without a SaaS account.

name: Perplexity AI
about: AI answer engine that searches and cites sources
description: Perplexity AI combines real-time web search with an AI language model to produce direct, cited answers to queries instead of a list of links. It positions itself as an alternative to traditional search for research and fact-finding tasks.

name: Photopea
about: Free browser-based Photoshop clone, no install needed
description: Photopea is a free, advanced image editor that runs entirely in the browser and supports native PSD, XD, Sketch, and Figma files alongside its own editing tools. It replicates most of Photoshop's core workflow — layers, masks, filters — making it a strong option for anyone who needs occasional PSD editing without a Creative Cloud subscription.

name: Pi Agent Harness
about: Minimal extensible terminal coding-agent harness
description: Pi is a lightweight harness for building and running terminal coding agents with a small core and plug-in tools. Developers reach for it when they want agent ergonomics without the weight of a full IDE or platform like OpenHands.

name: PimEyes
about: Reverse image search engine specifically for faces
description: PimEyes performs facial-recognition-based reverse image search, finding other photos of a matched face across the indexed web. It carries significant privacy and stalking misuse potential — meaningfully higher risk than infrastructure-focused OSINT tools — and should be used only for legitimate, authorized purposes such as checking your own online exposure.

name: Pipiri
about: Picture-in-picture for any macOS window, not just video
description: Pipiri turns any window or region into an always-on-top PiP panel across Spaces, aimed at terminals, agent UIs, dashboards, and videos without native PiP. Official site is lowtechguys.com/pipiri.

name: Plash
about: Puts any website on your Mac desktop as wallpaper
description: Plash renders a webpage as your macOS desktop background — dashboards, clocks, or anything with a URL. It is a tiny utility in the same odd-useful spirit as WindowSwap.

name: Privacy Flip
about: Turns off camera, mic, and radios when the Android screen locks
description: Privacy Flip disables camera, microphone, Bluetooth, and similar sensors when you lock the phone and can restore them on unlock. Search disable camera on lock android or privacy sensors.

name: Privacy.com
about: Virtual card numbers for safer online payments
description: Privacy.com generates virtual, single-use or merchant-locked card numbers linked to a real bank account, letting users shop online without exposing their actual card details. It's used to prevent recurring charges, limit fraud exposure, and control subscription spending.

name: Public APIs
about: Massive curated directory of free public APIs
description: Public APIs is a community-maintained list of free APIs across weather, finance, games, government data, and hundreds of other categories. Developers treat it like a phone book when prototyping integrations without hunting forums for endpoints.

name: PublicWWW
about: Search engine for source code across public websites
description: PublicWWW indexes the source code of millions of websites, letting users search for specific code snippets, tracking scripts, or embedded widgets to find every site using them. It's used for competitive research, tracking adoption of scripts, and OSINT investigations.

name: Purge
about: Open-source Mac cache and junk cleaner that moves files to Trash
description: Purge scans and cleans macOS system caches, developer build artifacts, and application junk using an open-source allowlist. It runs from the menu bar and defaults to moving deleted items to the Trash rather than permanently deleting them, ensuring nothing is lost by accident.

name: Python for Everybody
about: Free, university-affiliated introductory Python course
description: Python for Everybody (py4e) is a free, widely-used introductory Python programming course created by Dr. Charles Severance, covering fundamentals through data structures and basic web/data work. It's a common starting point for self-taught programmers and students with no prior coding background.

name: Qdrant
about: Rust vector database for similarity search, OSS and cloud
description: Qdrant is a vector database optimized for semantic search, recommendations, and RAG retrieval at scale. Developers choose it when embeddings need a fast, filter-rich store with both a self-hosted OSS path and a managed cloud option.

name: Quick, Draw!
about: Google's AI doodle-guessing game that learns from your drawings
description: Quick, Draw! is a Google AI experiment where you sketch a prompted object and a neural network tries to guess it in real time, with every drawing contributed back into a public dataset used to train recognition models. It's AutoDraw's sister experiment — game and data-collection rather than a practical drawing tool.

name: QuickTile Settings
about: Quick Settings tiles for Private DNS, USB debugging, and more
description: QuickTile Settings adds Android Quick Settings tiles for system toggles such as Private DNS hostnames and USB debugging. Search private dns tile or quick settings android developer tiles.

name: Quill
about: Ultra-minimal local macOS meeting recorder with on-device transcription
description: Quill is a tiny macOS app that records meetings and transcribes them entirely on-device with no account or cloud upload. It sits between FluidVoice-style dictation and Otter-style cloud meeting notes for users who want meeting capture without leaving the Mac.

name: Radiant
about: Local Mac UI for chatting with coding agents and watching tool calls
description: Radiant is a Mac coding harness with chat across cloud and local models and a live activity feed of tool calls. Search mac coding agent ui or local harness; Orca and DeepSeek Harness cover other shapes of the same job.

name: Radio Garden
about: Spin a 3D globe and listen to live radio stations worldwide
description: Radio Garden lets users spin an interactive globe and tune into live radio broadcasts from thousands of stations around the world in real time. Unlike Radiooooo's curated-by-era approach, it streams actual live radio by geographic location.

name: Radiooooo
about: Pick a decade and country, hear music from that era and place
description: Radiooooo is a musical time machine: pick a country on a map and a decade, and it plays curated music from that place and period. It's built for musical discovery and exploration rather than mainstream streaming.

name: Rascal
about: Keyboard-first Finder replacement with dual panes and vim keys
description: Rascal is a native macOS file manager with dual panes, a command palette, vim keys, and a disk treemap. It is for people who want Finder to keep up with keyboard-driven work.

name: reimagine-it
about: Restyles existing HTML from the content already in the file
description: reimagine-it is a CLI and agent skill that takes HTML in and emits a stronger standalone page using nouns, dates, and colors already in the document, offline, no extra design system. Search restyle html or content-derived design.

name: Reminders Menubar
about: Apple Reminders in the Mac menu bar
description: Reminders Menubar shows and completes Apple Reminders from the menu bar without opening the Reminders app. Search reminders menu bar mac; installable via Homebrew cask.

name: Remove.bg
about: One-click AI background removal from images
description: Remove.bg uses AI to automatically detect and remove the background from an uploaded image in seconds, producing a clean cutout without manual masking. It's widely used by e-commerce sellers, designers, and anyone needing quick transparent-background images.

name: RoomGPT
about: Upload a room photo, AI generates a redesigned version in seconds
description: RoomGPT uses AI to redesign a photo of any room into different styles — modern, minimalist, industrial, and more — giving an instant visual concept without hiring a designer. It's used for renovation inspiration and quick interior-design mockups.

name: rta-smriti-brain
about: Local-first project memory for AI coding agents
description: rta-smriti-brain is a local, evidence-aware memory layer so coding agents can recall project facts without a hosted brain service. Search coding agent memory or local agent knowledge graph.

name: Runway
about: AI creative suite for generating and editing video, images, and audio
description: Runway is a browser-based creative suite for generating and editing video, images, and audio around their Gen video models. It is aimed at filmmakers and teams who want generation inside a full editing workspace rather than a single-shot prompt box.

name: RustDesk
about: Open-source remote desktop software, a TeamViewer/AnyDesk alternative
description: RustDesk is a self-hostable, open-source remote desktop application for accessing and controlling computers remotely, built as a privacy-respecting alternative to TeamViewer and AnyDesk.

name: Sci-Hub
about: Shadow library providing free access to paywalled academic papers
description: Sci-Hub bypasses academic publisher paywalls to provide free access to millions of research papers, operating in direct legal conflict with copyright holders in most jurisdictions and facing ongoing takedown litigation. Include and use with that legal risk understood.

name: Scientific Agent Skills
about: Skill pack that turns an AI agent into a working scientist
description: Scientific Agent Skills is a large library of validated agent skills for biology, chemistry, and related sciences. Researchers install the pack so coding agents can run domain workflows instead of generic web search.

name: Scribe
about: Auto-generates step-by-step how-to guides by recording your screen actions
description: Scribe records a user's clicks and actions in the browser or desktop and automatically turns them into a step-by-step how-to guide with screenshots and instructions. It's used by teams to quickly document processes and onboarding without manual screenshotting and writing.

name: Scriberr
about: Self-hosted offline transcription with chat over your recordings
description: Scriberr is a self-hostable app that transcribes audio and video locally with Whisper or Parakeet, then lets you search and chat with the transcript. It is the full meeting-archive alternative to cloud tools like Otter.ai for people who want recordings to stay on their own server.

name: Scriptc
about: Vercel Labs experimental TypeScript-to-native compiler
description: Scriptc from Vercel Labs is an experimental compiler that turns TypeScript into native binaries, exploring a faster path than Node for CLI tools and agents. It is early infrastructure for developers, not a consumer-facing app.

name: SearXNG
about: Privacy metasearch that aggregates engines without tracking
description: SearXNG is a self-hostable metasearch engine that queries many search providers and returns merged results without profiling you. Privacy researchers and OSINT users run it as a Google alternative that does not build a behavioral profile.

name: Securo
about: Self-hosted personal finance manager
description: Securo is an open-source personal finance app you self-host to track accounts, budgets, and spending without handing financial data to a SaaS. It fills the budget-app gap next to Privacy.com, which handles virtual cards rather than full money management.

name: Semantica
about: Graph-native context and accountability layer for agent stacks
description: Semantica builds knowledge and context graphs with decision provenance so agent outputs can be traced to sources and reasoning steps. It sits under frameworks like LangChain as infrastructure for auditable, graph-grounded agents rather than opaque chat replies.

name: Shizuku
about: Lets normal Android apps call privileged APIs via ADB or root
description: Shizuku starts a privileged Java process so other apps can use system APIs without each one asking for root. It is the official bridge behind a large set of Android power-user tools (installers, debloaters, tile apps).

name: ShizuTools
about: Toolkit of Android system utilities powered by Shizuku
description: ShizuTools bundles debloat, app volume, downgrade, and other system controls that talk to Android through Shizuku. Search shizuku tools or android debloat without full root.

name: Shockwave
about: Local markdown notes with a baked-in coding agent and GitHub sync
description: Shockwave is a desktop notes app where your vault stays plain markdown on disk, syncs through your own GitHub repo, and includes an embedded coding agent. It targets note-takers who want Obsidian-like files plus agent memory without a separate Claude Code window.

name: Shodan
about: Search engine for internet-connected devices and IoT infrastructure
description: Shodan is a search engine that indexes internet-connected devices — servers, webcams, industrial control systems, routers — rather than webpages, based on banner data collected via scanning. It's a core OSINT and security research tool for finding exposed systems, and carries dual-use risk if misused against unauthorized targets.

name: Silex
about: Open-source no-code website builder that exports clean HTML/CSS
description: Silex is an open-source, browser-based website builder with free-form visual editing that exports clean, portable HTML/CSS instead of locking you into a proprietary platform. It's aimed at designers and developers who want no-code building without giving up ownership of the output.

name: Skiplagged
about: Finds cheaper flights via hidden-city ticketing
description: Skiplagged searches for cheaper airfare using hidden-city ticketing — booking a connecting flight and skipping the final leg — a practice that can save significant money but violates most airlines' terms of service and can lead to penalties like frequent-flyer account suspension. Use with that risk understood.

name: sloptrim
about: Agent skill that detects and trims AI-writing patterns in prose
description: sloptrim is an offline-oriented skill that flags telltale AI phrasing and helps agents tighten drafts before humans read them. Writers install it when agent-generated copy needs a pass for voice and credibility, not just grammar.

name: SpaceHey
about: MySpace-style retro social network revival
