description: SpaceHey recreates the look and feel of mid-2000s MySpace, letting users build customizable profile pages and connect with friends in a nostalgic, retro social network format. It's aimed at users who want an alternative to modern algorithm-driven social platforms.

name: Squoosh
about: Browser-based image compression tool with before/after comparison
description: Squoosh, built by Google, compresses images directly in the browser using multiple codecs, with a live before/after slider to compare quality and file size. It runs entirely client-side, so images never leave the user's device.

name: Stirling PDF
about: Self-hosted PDF toolkit you run on your own machine
description: Stirling PDF is a locally hosted suite for merging, splitting, converting, OCR, and otherwise editing PDFs in the browser. It is the self-hosted alternative to web PDF sites and Acrobat when files should not leave your network.

name: Suno
about: Generate a full song with music and vocals from a text prompt
description: Suno generates complete songs — instrumentals and vocals — from a text prompt describing genre, mood, and lyrics, turning a short description into a finished track in under a minute. Its training data and output have drawn copyright controversy from the music industry; use with that legal risk understood.

name: Supercook
about: Enter ingredients you have, get matching recipes
description: Supercook lets users list ingredients currently on hand and returns recipes that can be made with them, minimizing extra grocery trips. It's a practical kitchen tool for reducing food waste and simplifying meal planning.

name: Swift Salamander
about: Dual-pane file manager for macOS
description: Swift Salamander is a native dual-pane Mac file manager in active development. Search dual-pane Finder or Commander-style browsing on Mac; Rascal is the keyboard/vim-first alternative already listed.

name: SwitchYard
about: NVIDIA Rust LLM proxy that routes and translates agent API formats
description: SwitchYard is an NVIDIA NeMo project that proxies LLM traffic between OpenAI, Anthropic, and local backends so coding agents can speak their native API while the request lands on vLLM, NIM, or Ollama. It overlaps LiteLLM but focuses on agent protocol translation and benchmarking.

name: Tappie
about: Native GUI for Homebrew on Mac and Linux
description: Tappie is a graphical frontend for Homebrew so you can browse, install, and update formulae and casks without the terminal. It covers the full package set, not just GUI casks, with a native Mac app and a Linux edition.

name: tastemaker
about: Agent skills for taste and design direction
description: tastemaker is a skill pack that steers agents toward cohesive visual taste — palette, type pairing, and layout rhythm — instead of generic template aesthetics. It helps when you care as much about vibe as about working code.

name: terminal-browser
about: Real Chromium browser that runs inside the terminal
description: terminal-browser embeds a full Chromium instance in the terminal so you can browse the modern web from SSH or a TTY without leaving the shell. It is a niche CLI curiosity for remote servers and keyboard-first workflows.

name: Tesseract OCR
about: Classic open-source optical character recognition engine
description: Tesseract is the long-standing open-source OCR engine maintained by Google, used to extract text from scanned documents and images. It underpins countless PDF, scan, and accessibility pipelines and remains the default self-hosted OCR choice.

name: The FBI Vault
about: FBI's public reading room of declassified and FOIA-released documents
description: The FBI Vault is the Bureau's official electronic reading room, hosting declassified files, FOIA-released documents, and historical records on cases, individuals, and events. It's a primary-source research tool for journalists, historians, and the curious public.

name: The True Size Of
about: Drag countries around a map to see their true relative size
description: The True Size Of lets you drag any country over the map to compare its actual land area against others, correcting for the size distortion caused by the standard Mercator projection. It's a simple, effective educational tool for understanding real geographic scale.

name: The Useless Web
about: One button sends you to a random weird or funny website
description: The Useless Web is a novelty site built around a single button that teleports you to a random, often bizarre or pointless corner of the internet. It has no functional purpose beyond entertainment and rediscovering the internet's weirder, more chaotic side.

name: This Person Does Not Exist
about: Generates a new AI face of a person who doesn't exist, every refresh
description: This Person Does Not Exist uses a generative adversarial network (StyleGAN) to produce a photorealistic human face that isn't a real person, generating a new one on every page load. It's a widely cited demo of generative AI's image capabilities and is used in design, research, and privacy-related mockups.

name: TimesFM
about: Google's pretrained time-series foundation model for forecasting
description: TimesFM is a time-series foundation model from Google Research for zero-shot and fine-tuned forecasting. Search time series forecasting model or timesfm.

name: TinyWow
about: Free bundle of PDF, image, video, and AI mini-tools
description: TinyWow offers a large collection of free single-purpose tools for converting, compressing, and editing PDFs, images, and videos, alongside a growing set of AI writing and generation tools. It's a practical swiss-army-knife site for quick one-off file tasks without installing software.

name: TLDR Radio
about: Turns TLDR newsletters into a local podcast without an LLM
description: TLDR Radio ingests TLDR tech newsletters and turns them into a personal podcast feed you can listen to offline. It is a quirky audio utility for people who never finish reading newsletter digests but will listen on a walk.

name: TopShelf
about: Float websites and mini-apps as always-on-top windows from the Mac menu bar
description: TopShelf pins any website, web app, or built-in utility (such as notes, calculator, or pomodoro) into a lightweight always-on-top window that stays visible across full-screen spaces. It lets users keep reference docs, AI chats, and quick tools accessible without window juggling.

name: Typeform
about: Hosted conversational forms and surveys
description: Typeform builds one-question-at-a-time forms, quizzes, and surveys with a polished hosted editor. It is the usual search result for online forms; OpnForm is the open-source alternative already listed.

name: Unsplash
about: Free high-resolution stock photos, no attribution required
description: Unsplash is a massive library of free, high-resolution stock photography contributed by photographers worldwide. Images can be used for personal or commercial projects without mandatory attribution, making it a go-to source for designers, marketers, and developers needing quality visuals fast.

name: VirusTotal
about: Scans files and URLs against 70+ antivirus engines at once
description: VirusTotal aggregates dozens of antivirus engines and website scanners to check whether a file or URL is malicious. Security researchers, IT admins, and cautious users upload suspicious files or links to get a consolidated verdict rather than relying on a single antivirus product.

name: Vorssaint
about: Modular open-source menu-bar toolkit for Mac
description: Vorssaint is a local-first Mac menu-bar app you assemble from modules — switcher, clipboard, cleaner, and more — instead of installing a dozen one-trick utilities. Install only the pieces you use.

name: Wayback Machine
about: View archived snapshots of almost any webpage across time
description: The Wayback Machine, run by the Internet Archive, has archived hundreds of billions of webpages since the 1990s and lets anyone view how a site looked on a given date. It's essential for research, journalism, verifying claims, and recovering content from dead or changed websites.

name: WhisperX
about: Local Whisper transcription with word-level timestamps
description: WhisperX wraps OpenAI Whisper with forced alignment and speaker-aware timestamps for accurate local transcripts. Researchers and tool builders run it when Otter-style SaaS is too closed and vanilla Whisper timestamps are too loose.

name: Wick
about: Reading-focus tool that dims the Mac screen around a spotlight
description: Wick dims everything except a movable reading area so you can focus on one region of the screen. Search focus reading mac or dim screen spotlight.

name: Wigle
about: Crowd-sourced WiFi network and geolocation database
description: Wigle is a crowd-sourced database mapping WiFi networks and cell towers worldwide, built from user-submitted wardriving data, letting anyone look up the physical location tied to a WiFi SSID or BSSID. It's a well-known OSINT and security research tool with the usual dual-use privacy considerations.

name: WindowSwap
about: Watch a live-style video of the view from a stranger's window
description: WindowSwap shows a video of the view from someone's window somewhere in the world, swapped randomly on each visit. It's a quiet, meditative novelty site built around shared perspective rather than utility.

name: Windy
about: Interactive weather map with wind, rain, and wave layers
description: Windy is a highly visual, interactive weather forecasting map that layers wind patterns, precipitation, waves, temperature, and more onto a zoomable globe. It's popular with pilots, sailors, and outdoor enthusiasts who need more granular, visual weather data than a standard forecast app provides.

name: Wisp
about: Menu-bar scratchpad for Mac, summon with a hotkey
description: Wisp is a dead-simple Mac scratchpad in the menu bar (Option-Space by default) that stores plain markdown and can sync via iCloud or any folder. Search mac scratchpad or menu bar notes; brew install --cask wisp.

name: WolframAlpha
about: Computational engine that answers by computing, not searching
description: WolframAlpha is a computational knowledge engine that solves math problems, analyzes data, and answers factual queries by computing answers from curated data and algorithms rather than searching indexed web pages. It's widely used by students and researchers for step-by-step math solutions and quick scientific or statistical lookups.

name: youtube-subscriptions-ingest
about: Pulls YouTube subscriptions into a cross-linked knowledge graph
description: This ingest pipeline turns YouTube subscription metadata into a linked graph for a second-brain vault. Search youtube subscriptions obsidian, knowledge graph, or second brain youtube.

name: Zapier
about: Connects thousands of apps with automated no-code workflows
description: Zapier is a hosted automation platform that wires 9,000+ apps together with trigger-action workflows, so a form response can create a task, ping Slack, or update a spreadsheet without custom code. n8n covers the same job as a self-hosted, code-friendly alternative.
